al_winter_wall.blurb: A short stretch of sandstone cliff at the Jamestown crag in northeast Alabama, on the tail of Lookout Mountain. The wall holds about a dozen lines, nearly all of them traditional with a couple of bolted sport routes. Grades start around 5.7 and run to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, so it suits climbers comfortable placing their own gear on moderate to stiff lines. Walk the trail beneath Harvest Wall next door and keep going until a right-facing corner rises toward a roof. Seepage keeps parts of the cliff damp for days after rain, so pick a dry spell.

al_hurricane_creek_park.blurb: A small, family-oriented crag in a wooded gorge outside Cullman, roughly half an hour from Birmingham. The sandstone here is short and gentle: about ten climbs, with a handful of boulder problems from V0 to V2 and roped lines from 5.6 up to 5.9, split across top-rope, sport and trad. Most roped climbing is set up from the cliff top, and the climbs sit close to a creekside picnic area at the bottom of a descent trail. It is a good spot for newer climbers to try real rock, and plenty of unclimbed rock remains across the creek.

al_turtle_rock_area_slabolicious_block.blurb: One of the boulder clusters near the tin-roof shelter at Horse Pens 40, the sandstone bouldering park in Steele that is known for sloper holds and tricky top-outs. This block carries about ten problems with a wide spread: a pair of easy ones near V0 and V1, a solid middle of V4 to V6, and several harder problems up to V8, including low-start variations. It is a better stop for climbers who already climb V4 or above than for first-timers. Expect friction-dependent moves, and note that fall and winter give the best grip.
